also: which season do you like best?

terms.grammar: tempus, temporis n. with the genitive annī
evidence: Caes. BG 1.54: mātūrius paulō quam tempus annī postulābat (Lewis & Short s.v. tempus)
Cic. Rep. 1.18: erat hībernum tempus annī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin has no single word for a season: it says “time of the year”, and names the four as spring, summer, autumn and winter (vēr, aestās, autumnus, hiems).

phrases.latin: «Bene ēmistī,» inquit avus. «Hōc annī tempore vīlia sunt māla.»
phrases.english: “That’s a bargain,” said Grandpa. “Apples are cheap at this time of year.”

phrases.latin: Quod tempus annī tibi maximē placet?
phrases.english: Which season do you like best?

sources: Lewis & Short: tempus · Lewis & Short: annus
